page: Hetzner Cloud cx43 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs with a shared CPU allocation, 8 physical cores, and 1.0 thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 16.0 GB of RAM, which equates to approximately 1.95 GB per core. Storage is provided via a 160 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance runs on the QEMU hypervisor. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

In benchmark evaluations, the cx43 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2548.38, placing it in the top 25%. However, its multi-core performance falls into the average range, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 20252.78 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7324.0. Memory bandwidth is moderate, measuring 89.3 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 62.62 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Single-threaded gzip compression is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 23.39 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performs at an average level of 70.74 GB/sec.

The shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, predictable multi-core performance, as resource contention may occur. Despite this, the server maintains average performance across database operations (6708.71 on PassMark) and Redis SET operations (14.46 million operations per second). It is also capable of handling light LLM inference, processing 1073.74 tokens per second for a 135M model prompt, though performance drops to a weak 31.68 tokens per second for a 7B model prompt. This hardware profile is suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, static web serving, and development environments that benefit from a high vCPU-to-RAM ratio without requiring dedicated CPU threads.
description: Hetzner Cloud cx43 is an x86_64 virtual server configured with 8 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 16.0 GB of RAM, and 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the QEMU hypervisor, this instance delivers strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 2548.38 in stress-ng tests, while maintaining average multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention, making it less optimal for sustained high-load multi-threaded tasks, as reflected in its average Geekbench multi-core score of 7324.0. However, with solid database operations and static web serving throughput, the cx43 is a cost-efficient option for development environments, software compilation, and moderate web serving workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources or public IPv4 addresses.
